questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had never been to Australia before, so going on an exchange there was just super convenient.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was super good, I got to meet a bunch of new friends as well as expereince what it's like to study in another country.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The university was really good at informing the exchange students about everything worht knokwing. This meant a lot of emails and messages, but they were really good at equipping you for what was about to happen.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Because I lived a college near the university that meant that I got a free shuttle from the airport to my college when I arrived. That was super nice since I had been on the go for 24 hours prior to arrival.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There were a couple of colleges.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: My college was 100% catered, meaning all meals were cooked by professional staff.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It's definetly worth trying. People are so friendly and welcoming, and it's so convenient living 2 minutes from all your classes.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Once you get your institution relevant email everything is so straight forward and if you dont think it is, there's a ton of videos that guide you through the process.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Vidoes, and the exchange office which you could call or email.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Register as fast a possible, idk.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses were a lot easier than doing them at KU (University of Copenhagen).

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was way worse, as a science student, chalk blackboard lectures are so underestimated. All my lectures were taught using powerpoints slideshows which should be a felony. So I'm looking forward to chalk and blackboards lectures at KU once again.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Mathematical Modelling and differential equations, Advanced quantum mechanic and optics, Obervational Astrophysics, and Introdcution to bio.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Advanded quatum mechanics and optics was a really interesting course and the way quantum mechanics was potrayed was way different than at KU, I really liked that. Other than that, mathematical modelling had some fun assignments that were not to difficult but just fun to play around with.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Nothing really.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The college accomodation was more expensive than anticipated. But since it was catered it kinda makes sense.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Almost every sport you could think of was somewhat represented with either a court, field or whatever. So wahtever you felt like doing you could almost always do it. The gym on campus was also really good.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Boat parties in the Sydney harbour is a must!! I went on a couple and it's an insane experience (expensive but defo worth it)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Australia is crazy big, but domestic flights a pretty cheap outside the school holiday periods. So you should defo go to some of the other cities while in Sydney if you can afford it.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Living at colleges is the best way. Cause 80% of poeple at colleges are from Australia and they are so welcoming and nice.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The fact that they are so welcoming and always want to help is just insane.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be open minded. Prioritize going to social events over homework (to a certain extent) cause you can always catch up with your academic work in the exam period, but you wont have unlimited invitations to parties and so on.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Enjoy it! Cause once it's over you'll miss it like crazy.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being open minded and not judging people before actually talking to them.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge was leaving everyone and saying goodbye. Sheesh that still sucks...

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
